question: What is the rate of tax collected at source when I buy an overseas tour package for Rs 12 lakh?
reference: 2% of the amount, with no threshold (Section 394(1) Table, Sl. No. 8).

extra.old_reference: Footnote 89 (p.472): 5% up to ten lakh rupees; 20% above ten lakh rupees.

question: Can I deduct the interest on a loan I took to buy shares from my dividend income?
reference: No. No deduction at all is allowed against dividend income or income from the listed mutual fund units (Section 93(2)).

extra.old_reference: Footnote 10c (p.127): interest was deductible, limited to 20% of the dividend income.

question: What happens if a business does not get its accounts audited when the Act requires it?
phrases: Rs. 75000 for a delay up to one month
reference: A fee under Section 428(c): Rs 75,000 for a delay of up to one month, and Rs 1,50,000 after that.

extra.old_reference: Footnote 10 (p.532), old Section 446: a penalty of 0.5% of turnover or gross receipts, or Rs 1,50,000, whichever is less.

question: What is the fee for filing a statement of financial transaction late?
phrases: for every day for which such failure continues and such fee shall not exceed a sum of Rs. 1,00,000
reference: Rs 200 for every day the failure continues, up to Rs 1,00,000 (Section 427(3)). If it is still not filed after a notice, a penalty of Rs 1,000 a day, up to Rs 1,00,000 (Section 454).

extra.old_reference: Footnote 12 (p.540), old Section 454(1): a penalty of Rs 500 for every day.

question: What is the punishment for wilfully trying to evade more than Rs 60 lakh of tax?
phrases: simple imprisonment for a term up to two years, or with fine, or with both
reference: Simple imprisonment of up to two years, or a fine, or both, because the amount is above Rs 50 lakh (Section 478(1)(a)).

extra.old_reference: Footnote 24 (p.564): rigorous imprisonment of six months to seven years, and a fine, above Rs 25 lakh.

question: Is TDS deducted on interest paid on a Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal compensation to an individual?
phrases: (iv) on the compensation amount awarded by a Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal
reference: No. For an individual, no TDS is deducted on this interest, whatever the amount (Section 393(4) Table, Sl. No. 7, item (iv)(A)). The amount limit applies only to persons other than individuals.

extra.old_reference: Footnote 83 (p.470): no TDS only if the interest was at most Rs 50,000 in the tax year, for everyone.
